messages:
Marta L: FYI — we're seeing a large tail latency increase on SSE responses since the API proto change rolled out last night. Rollout paused.
Kevin H: saw it on the dashboards too. 95th/99th for eventstream spikes 2-3x. Any obvious suspects?
Ryan C: CI perf failed on the canary, but the e2e alerts were noisy so it got merged. I started a quick bisect on the staging deploys.
perf-bot: perf/regression report: https://perf.internal/reports/1960001240 — overall token p95 +120ms, p99 +380ms, top regressions: serialization, sse_flush, toolcall-overhead. :warning:
Kevin H: I profiled a staging trace and the hot path is serialize_tool_payload -> sse_frame_build -> sse_write. serialize_tool_payload is doing an extra copy of the KV cache payload now.
Lina P: that matches my local reproducer — when tool-call attachments are present we materialize a combined blob and memcpy it per-chunk. Before the proto change we streamed attachments as shared refs.
Ryan C: timeline: PR #4123 added the new api event header + attachment bundling to simplify clients. Looks tiny in code but changes how we construct SSE frames.
Marta L: can we get the bisect result? If it's that PR it's a quick revert.
Kevin H: bisect pointing to PR #4123. Quick diff: we switched from incremental writer to build-then-serialize to support new header ordering.
Lina P: small snippet from the trace:
```
0.38s serialize_tool_payload (memcpy x3)
0.22s sse_frame_build
0.12s sse_write
0.08s kernel_select
0.06s kv_fetch (miss)
```
Notice memcpy x3 when attachments present.
Ryan C: also saw more KV cache misses in the same traces — bundling changes increased payload size so KV keys were evicted faster in the short-lived cache.
Marta L: so two contributing factors: (1) serialize-change causes extra memcopies; (2) larger frames => more KV churn => more fetches.
Kevin H: quick mitigation options:
- revert PR #4123 (fast)
- rework writer to stream attachments (better long-term)
- increase KV cache size / adjust eviction policy temporarily
I think revert + follow-up patch is fastest to un-block rollout.
Lina P: agree. I can prototype a streaming-writer in a patch but need a day.
deploy-bot: started rollback: reverting commit 7f8a3b2 (PR #4123) to canary.
perf-bot: re-run perf check on canary after revert: https://perf.internal/reports/1960001260
Kevin H: can we also add a unit test guard against switching to build-then-serialize for SSE frames? This pattern keeps biting us.
Marta L: yes — add an integ test that simulates attachments and asserts no more than 1 memcpy for streaming path.
Ryan C: CI accepted revert; canary perf back to baseline: p95 down ~110ms, p99 down ~360ms. Rollout unblocked.
Marta L: thanks all. Action items:
- Lina: prototype streaming-writer (PR by EOD)
- Kevin: add test + perf regression guard
- Ryan: follow up on temporary KV cache config tweak for big payloads
- Ops: monitor SSE p99 for next 24h
perf-bot: noted actions in ticket PERF-7204.
Marta L: filing postmortem notes in #incidents, will include traces and bisect steps. :memo:
